subject: SLA-aware GPU mix + prompt breadth survey for dedicated sizing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA-aware GPU mix + prompt breadth survey for dedicated sizing

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To get our dedicated sizing team a concrete starting point, can you please fill the small sample set below or share a short telemetry extract? The goal is to recommend a GPU mix (A100 vs A800-ish skus), reserved pool size, and a burst plan that meets your target latency SLOs without over-committing.

Quick asks (feel free to paste CSV snippets):
1) Typical prompt token distribution (percentiles or histogram): mean prompt tokens, p50, p90, p99.
2) Response length distribution: mean/median tokens, tail p95/p99 response tokens.
3) Concurrent sessions typical and peak (concurrency measured as active KV sessions).
4) Average session duration and session stickiness (how long does a user keep a session open / re-use context).
5) Traffic shape: sustained RPS and typical burst windows (e.g., 30s burst of Xx sustained RPS). Indicate dayparting if traffic varies by hour.
6) SLO targets: p95 & p99 latency targets for interactive calls, and acceptable fallback model latency if primary unavailable.
7) Any heavy multimodal steps (image/video) or tool-calls that create long tail response times.

If you have sample rows, just attach a CSV named novamed_token_sample.csv. We’ll run a quick traffic synthesis and reply with a recommended fleet mix and occupancy hypothesis within 48 hours.

I attached our short preflight checklist and an example burst-window visualization for reference.

Next steps: once we get the telemetry, Marissa will run a sizing pass and I’ll propose a two-stage reserved plan (baseline + burst pool) and a canary routing policy.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Pre-Sales — Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf, slo-burst-window.png

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA-aware GPU mix + prompt breadth survey for dedicated sizing

Jonas —

Thanks, appreciate the clear list. Attaching a small sample export (anonymized) and a quick note below. We also looped procurement on the thread to get ahead of PO timing.

High level:
- Prompt tokens: mean 28, p50 24, p90 68, p99 200
- Response tokens: mean 160, p50 120, p90 420, p99 1200 (long-generation assistant reports)
- Typical concurrency: 85 active sessions sustained; peak bursts up to 1,200 concurrent over ~45s windows (observed during product email pushes)
- Average session duration: 12 minutes; many sessions are short (single-turn) but about 12% persist > 30m for multi-turn care conversations
- Traffic shape: weekday daytime spike between 09:00–11:30 PST, smaller spike 15:00–16:00 PST; ~3:1 daypart ratio
- SLO: target p95 <= 500ms token-latency for interactive prompts and p99 <= 1.2s. For long generations we can tolerate p95 <= 1.5s.
- No heavy multimodal inference currently; occasional third-party tool calls do not change token counts.

I've attached novamed_token_sample.csv with 10k anonymized rows from last month and included our procurement contact.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform — NovaMed AI
attachments: novamed_token_sample.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA-aware GPU mix + prompt breadth survey for dedicated sizing

Alex —

Thanks for the sample — good signals. I ran a quick pass locally to sketch occupancy and recommended GPU mix. High-level hypotheses below; I’ll follow up with a more formal spreadsheet and a short call to validate assumptions.

Initial sizing notes (back-of-envelope):
- Token profile suggests heavy tail; p99 response token ~1200 increases memory pressure for KV cache during long generations.
- For interactive SLOs (p95 <= 500ms) we recommend a mixed pool: majority high-memory A100/A800-style instances for KV-heavy, long-context sessions, and a small fleet of cheaper T4-equivalent for short, high-throughput single-turn inference (cost-savings routing).
- Baseline reserved capacity: target to sustain 100 concurrent interactive sessions with headroom (20% reserve) -> recommend capacity to host ~120 active sessions on primary pool.
- Burst pool: allow auto-burst to an elastic pool sized for additional 1,100 concurrent sessions for 60s windows using preemptible/spot-like capacity with automatic fallback model routing.
- Suggested quantization: run Medium-quality 8-bit quantized variant for most throughput; keep a full-precision variant for high-fidelity multi-turn threads.

Questions / assumptions to validate on a quick call (15–20m):
1) Are the long-generation workloads tolerant of reduced precision for tail-quality?
2) Do you want sticky session affinity (session pinned to same host) or can we treat sessions as stateless with KV cache warming via prefix caching?
3) Acceptance of spot/ephemeral capacity for burst windows (savings vs risk tradeoff).

I’ll attach a preliminary cost sketch and a short occupancy spreadsheet after we confirm the answers. Available for a call Wednesday 9/21 10:00–11:00 PST if that works.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: initial-occupancy-sketch.xlsx (will send), redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf

From: Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA-aware GPU mix + prompt breadth survey for dedicated sizing

Hi Marissa / Jonas —

Thanks for the plan. A couple of procurement items to align before we proceed with a pilot:
- Contract term: prefer 9–12 months with a 30-day opt-out during pilot window.
- SLA credits: need clarity on p95/p99 measurement windows and remediation steps.
- Billing: monthly invoice with clear line items for baseline reserved capacity vs burst credits.

We’re happy to move forward with the proposed sizing as a pilot provided you can share:
1) A simple demo agreement template (we can review redlines)
2) The occupancy spreadsheet Marissa mentioned (so finance can model cost)
3) Example runbook for burst failover and model fallback behavior (we need this for internal auditors)

If you can send those three artifacts this week, we’ll circulate internally and aim to start pilot onboarding the week of 10/05.

Regards,
NovaMed Procurement
Procurement Team — NovaMed AI
